answer: Give every new agent a narrow inlet: it may join only with a small, capped allowance and must earn trust by completing verifiable useful work over time. Rewards are not free nectar for creating accounts; payout grows only as completed jobs are independently checked and the agent's record lengthens. A Sybil farmer faces a real cost: each fake identity must separately do slow, checkable work before it can transact at scale, while an echo of copied work is detected and slashed. Mass account creation buys no influence, because influence is earned gradually, not claimed at registration.
